schema.note: Feature-flow oracle table for driving the REAL kitchen-sink GUI app (Rust port) with real keyboard/mouse input via bin/ks-input. Every `sources` entry is file:line in this repo. Placeholders: `$HOME` expands to the sandbox HOME ($SANDBOX/home), so `~/notes` etc. resolve inside the sandbox. See Tests/app_flows.md for the runner contract (fixtures, input kinds, oracle kinds).
input_kinds: key SPEC  — one key chord/sequence, e.g. `cmd+k`, `ctrl+b w`, `ctrl+tab`, `cmd+shift+.`
type TEXT — type literal text into the focused field/editor (KS-Input must not interpret it)
click-rel FX FY — a click at fractions (0..1) of the window's content rect
wait MS — wait, then optionally take a checkpoint screenshot
do:VERB — a socket `do:` verb used as a step for features that have no keybinding
raw VERB — a raw socket verb (e.g. `reload`)
oracle_kinds: reply   {verb, error?, why?} — the reply a `do:` step in `steps` got: with `error`, it must be an error containing that text ("" = any error); without, it must not be an error
state   {path, after?, equals?, not_equals?, min?, contains?, contains_name?, length?, every_name_contains?} — read the daemon `state` JSON
disk    {path, glob?, contains?, exists?, is_dir?, count_min?} — a path (or glob) relative to the sandbox HOME
independent {describe} — a non-state recomputation the runner performs (ls / Python difflib / do: reply body)
visual  {after, expect} — a screenshot at `after`; a vision model decides (use only when no state/disk oracle exists)
log     {none_of:[...]} — the sandbox daemon.log must not contain any of these

One deterministic config for the whole table, applied to the sandbox copy of commands.toml ($SANDBOX/home/commands.toml) before the run: three known open notes, a fixed Files root, and a plain (non-nvim) notes editor so typing/save/find are deterministic without an external nvim process. Deterministic listing order for the sorting flow. The shipped [files] sort is created/desc (commands.toml:261-262), whose row order depends on fixture birth times; this makes it name/asc so the expected order is a property of the names, not the clock. Applied after cfg-sandbox (fixtures run in order) and only overrides sort/sort-order.
Unicode text pair: compare must line up and show the exact characters (no byte-index slicing / mojibake in TextSide decode or the row model).
One changed unicode line (日本語 → 日本語!) so the diff is exactly one section with 3 rows.
A multi-row diff section (b,c vs B,C) so "copy the current line" (Ctrl+Opt+R) is distinguishable from "copy the section" (Ctrl+R).
Second line of a two-line changed block; PRD-compare.md:308/411 promises Ctrl+Opt+R copies only the current line.
Empty side: 0 lines, 0 rows, 0 sections; Home/End/Ctrl+N/Ctrl+R must be safe no-ops.
Both sides empty: `summary` is the empty label and there is no phantom diff/edit.
Same file on both sides of the folder pair (counts.same == 1).
Same content as dirL/root.txt.
Nested file in the folder pair: the `sub` folder row is the one Return expands, and this file opens as the in-view text compare.
Differs from the left copy so the folder counts are different 1 / same 1 and the opened text pair has one section.

Scopes the three tool panels' outputs inside the sandbox HOME (disk oracles only resolve paths under $SANDBOX/home, never /tmp) and makes the Health Checks run deterministic: the text-table Markdown save and the Create File script write under ~/tt and ~/ff, and the health script appends one line per run so a re-run is countable. Applied after cfg-sandbox; all three keys already exist in the repo commands.toml ([text-table] save-dir:91, [filefast] save-dir:104, [health-checks] script:633).

A folder whose name contains several dots: renaming a *directory* must select the whole name (inline_rename.rs:7-17 is_dir branch), not a `stem` ending at the last dot, so typing `release` cannot produce `release.release`.
A multi-dot *file*: the inline rename selects the stem up to the last dot (`archive.tar`), so typing `bundle` must give `bundle.gz` — the extension is the last component only (files.rs:2102-2122).
Natural (number-aware) name sort: `Item 2.txt` must sort before `Item 10.txt` like Finder's localizedStandardCompare (list_filter.rs:317-325), unlike a plain string sort.
The other half of the numeric-collation pair; a lexicographic sort would put it first ('1' < '2').

import difflib,json,os,sys
h=os.environ["SBX_HOME"]
l=open(os.path.join(h,"compare","textL.txt"),encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()
r=open(os.path.join(h,"compare","textR.txt"),encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()
ops=[o for o in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None,l,r,autojunk=False).get_opcodes() if o[0]!="equal"]

c=((json.load(open(os.environ["STATE_FILE"])).get("compare") or {}).get("current") or {})
state_rows=sum(1 for x in (c.get("rows") or []) if x.get("kind")!="same")
sys.exit(0 if rows_n==state_rows and len(ops)==c.get("sections") else 1)
'
